breakfast.name: Boiled Fish and Grits
instructions: Season fish with lime, salt
Boil potatoes, onion, pepper, tomatoes, thyme, scotch bonnet
Add fish, cook until flaky
Cook grits separately with butter
Serve fish and broth over grits
breakfast.description: The Bahamian breakfast staple — tender fish in broth over creamy grits.

breakfast.name: Johnny Cake
instructions: Mix dry ingredients
Cut in butter, add milk and egg
Knead lightly
Shape into flat round
Bake at 180°C 20 min until golden
Slice and serve with butter
breakfast.description: A slightly sweet quick bread baked golden.

breakfast.name: Tuna and Grits
instructions: Cook grits with butter until creamy
Sauté onion, pepper, tomato
Add tuna, heat through
Serve tuna mixture over grits with hot sauce
breakfast.description: Quick Bahamian breakfast — sometimes made with fresh tuna seared rare, sometimes humble canned tuna. Both are good.

lunch.name: Conch Salad
instructions: Score and tenderize conch, dice small
Combine with all diced vegetables
Add citrus juices and scotch bonnet
Toss well, let marinate 15 min
Season with salt and pepper
lunch.description: Fresh, citrus-cured conch with crunchy vegetables — Bahamian ceviche.

lunch.name: Cracked Conch
instructions: Pound conch very thin
Dredge in flour, dip in beaten eggs, coat in breadcrumbs
Deep fry until golden and crispy
Drain on paper towels
Serve with lemon and hot sauce
lunch.description: Battered and fried conch — the quintessential Bahamian dish.

lunch.name: Bahamian Mac and Cheese
instructions: Cook macaroni until just al dente
Mix eggs, evaporated milk, mustard, seasonings
Layer in buttered baking dish: pasta, cheese, pasta, cheese
Pour egg-milk mixture over
Top with remaining cheese and paprika
Bake at 175°C for 35-40 min until golden and set — it should be firm enough to slice, not scoopable
lunch.description: Bahamian mac and cheese is baked dense and sliceable — more casserole than sauce. A mandatory side at every cookout and holiday.

dinner.name: Bahamian Stew Fish
instructions: Season fish with lime and salt
Brown fish in butter, set aside
Sauté onions, peppers, tomatoes
Add tomato paste, thyme, scotch bonnet
Return fish, add water to cover
Simmer 20 min until sauce thickens
dinner.description: Grouper steaks simmered in a rich tomato-onion sauce.

dinner.name: Peas and Rice with Baked Chicken
instructions: Season chicken, bake at 190°C 45 min
Cook rice with pigeon peas, coconut milk, onion, garlic, thyme, tomato paste
Simmer until rice is fluffy and liquid absorbed
Serve chicken over peas and rice
dinner.description: Coconut peas and rice with crispy baked chicken.

dinner.name: Steamed Souse (Chicken or Pig Feet)
instructions: Boil meat until very tender (45 min for chicken, longer for pig feet)
Add sliced onion, celery, pepper, allspice, bay leaf
Squeeze in lime juice generously
Season with salt and hot pepper
Simmer 15 more min — the broth should be clear and limey
Serve in bowls with the broth and a side of grits or Johnny cake
dinner.description: Saturday morning souse — a lime-and-allspice broth with tender meat. Every fish fry shack sells it alongside boiled fish.

snacks.name: Conch Fritters
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, salt
Add egg, milk, stir to batter
Fold in conch, onion, pepper, celery, hot sauce
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil
Fry until golden brown
Drain and serve with dipping sauce
snacks.description: Crispy, spicy conch fritters — a Bahamian must-have.

snacks.name: Scorched Conch
instructions: Score and tenderize fresh conch
Toss with lime juice, salt, diced onion, bird pepper
Eat raw immediately — no cooking
snacks.description: Raw conch with lime and fiery bird pepper — as fresh as Bahamian food gets. Eaten right at the dock.

snacks.name: Conch Salad (Raw Conch Ceviche)
ingredients: Juice of 6 Sour oranges (or 3 oranges + 3 limes)
instructions: Tenderize conch by scoring in a crosshatch pattern, then dice small
Dice all vegetables
Toss conch with vegetables in a bowl
Squeeze citrus juice over everything — the acid 'cooks' the conch
Add Scotch bonnet to taste
Season with salt
Let marinate 5-10 minutes (not too long or conch gets tough)
Serve in a cup on the beach — this is eaten standing up at fish fry shacks
The roadside conch salad makers are Nassau's most viral street food stars
snacks.description: The Bahamas' most famous street food — raw conch tossed with citrus and Scotch bonnet, made right in front of you at the fish fry. Went viral when tourists filmed the speed and knife skills of the roadside conch salad makers at Arawak Cay.

desserts.name: Guava Duff
ingredients: Sauce: 1/2 cup butter, 1 cup sugar, 2 eggs, rum
instructions: Mix dough: flour, butter, sugar, eggs, baking powder
Roll out, spread guava over dough
Roll up, wrap in cloth
Steam for 45 minutes
Make sauce: cream butter and sugar, add eggs and rum
Slice duff, pour warm sauce over
desserts.description: A steamed guava pudding with buttery rum sauce — the Bahamian dessert.

desserts.name: Benny Cake (Sesame Candy)
instructions: Toast sesame seeds until golden
Make sugar syrup to hard crack stage
Add sesame seeds and lime juice
Pour onto greased tray
Score into squares while warm, snap when cooled
desserts.description: Crunchy sesame candy — sold wrapped in wax paper at every Bahamian straw market.

drinks.name: Switcha (Limeade)
instructions: Juice limes
Mix with water and sugar
Stir until sugar dissolves
Serve over plenty of ice

drinks.name: Sky Juice (Gin and Coconut Water)
instructions: Crack fresh coconut, pour out water
Mix coconut water with gin to taste
Add splash of condensed milk
Grate nutmeg on top
Serve over ice
drinks.description: The unofficial drink of the Bahamas — gin in fresh coconut water.

drinks.name: Goombay Smash
instructions: Combine rums and juices over ice
Add grenadine
Shake or stir
Serve in tall glass with pineapple wedge
drinks.description: The Bahamas' signature cocktail — invented at Miss Emily's Blue Bee Bar in Green Turtle Cay. Sweet, strong, and dangerous in the sun.
